sources.title: Poor Charlie’s Almanack: The Wit and Wisdom of Charles T. Munger (expanded collection, HTML mirror)
sources.author: Charles T. Munger; collection edited by Peter D. Kaufman
sources.publisher: Retrieved publisher/host: CoffeeTalk101 on GitHub. Original collection publisher is not independently verified by the retrieved mirror.
sources.primaryStatus: Attributed first-person speeches embedded in an unofficial mirror; not authenticated against the publisher or recordings

sections.title: Harvard School Commencement Speech
sections.note: Inversion and active attention to disconfirming evidence. Date attribution belongs to the mirror.

sections.title: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom as It Relates to Investment Management and Business
sections.note: USC business talk. The mirror introduction says published by Outstanding Investor Digest May 5, 1995; speech year and publication year differ.

sections.title: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom, Revisited
sections.note: Stanford Law School; mirror introduction explicitly says the collection editor abridged passages and added comments.

sections.title: Academic Economics: Strengths and Faults after Considering Interdisciplinary Needs
sections.note: UC Santa Barbara economics lecture: opportunity cost, incentives, comparative advantage, higher-order consequences.

sections.title: The Psychology of Human Misjudgment
sections.note: The mirror describes a combined, revised text with new material, not a single delivered talk. It identifies an April 24, 1995 Cambridge Center for Behavioral Studies talk among antecedents. Do not label the 25-item revision an exact 1995 transcript.

limitations: Visible transcription/OCR errors, repeated text and disrupted headings occur. Exact wording and dates require an authorized edition or recording before publication.
One underlying collection; separate chapters do not constitute independent corroboration.
Retrieval and source anchors are verified; speech authenticity, rights and empirical psychology claims are not independently verified. No full source text is redistributed.
